title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has responded to the Committee’s 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its commitments to improve transparency, accountability, and public trust in AI systems. It plans to develop clearer standards, enhance regulation, and foster collaboration between industry, academia, and civil society to ensure AI technologies serve the public good.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting out how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in England’s qualifications system, aiming to keep exams fair, secure and reliable. The guidance responds to a request from key ministers and outlines standards and checks for schools and exam bodies that use AI tools.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright laws affect the use of copyrighted works in training AI systems, exploring legal, economic, and ethical implications. It evaluates the risks and benefits for creators, AI developers, and society, offering policy recommendations for balancing innovation and intellectual property protection.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report, “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its plans to address the committee’s concerns about safety, ethics, and regulation. It promises further policy action, increased support for research and innovation, and the development of regulatory frameworks to keep the UK at the forefront of responsible AI development.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee that will examine how artificial intelligence interacts with public standards. It also includes a FAQ section that explains key points and answers common questions about the committee’s work.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence, outlining its views on policy and regulatory matters. The submission aims to inform the committee’s review and recommendations for AI governance frameworks.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy examines how artificial intelligence will reshape rules for medical products, aiming to keep them safe and effective as new technology appears. It follows the guidance from the AI White Paper to set clear standards, assess risks, and establish transparent regulations for AI‑driven medical devices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑driven defence force in the world relative to its size. It seeks to use advanced AI to improve operational capabilities, decision‑making, and overall mission success.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport AI Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport industry to take advantage of artificial intelligence’s benefits while also tackling its potential risks. It lays out practical steps and strategies for safely and responsibly integrating AI into transport services.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report reviews how copyrighted materials are used to train and develop AI systems, looking at how these practices fit with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines the current state of compliance, highlights challenges, and offers recommendations to balance AI innovation with copyright protection.
